captureKind: Direct Unity Editor camera stills, 1920x1080. Same-scene anonymous leaf comparison; not native acceptance.
identityLimits: The Ward scene and ARK references are recognizable; only leaf-variant mapping is concealed. No claim of blind cross-game testing.
scoring: 0 missing/broken,1 severe,2 conspicuously artificial,3 credible progress with clear focal weaknesses,4 strong with minor remaining flaws,5 reference matched. Null is unqualified.

cam_hill.reason: A reads as living dark olive/green foliage and separates the oasis tree from the pale mineral basin. B reads silvery/gray with pale exterior clusters. A has a coherent shaded crown and preserves the same visible branch/crown outline.
cam_hill.remaining: A is still largely one dark olive family and muted inside; broad lower/inner clusters compress together. Raster edges remain noisy. This does not solve the surrounding paving, basin or sky.

cam_hero.reason: B reduces the washed-out pale fronts and presents green/yellow-green lit leaves against darker olive shade. This is more plausible foliage material than A at this close view. Bark and branch structure remain readable; no new gross silhouette loss is visible.
cam_hero.remaining: Dark foliage in the upper half loses separation and reads as dense mottled sheets in places. Fine edge quality remains visibly stepped/noisy, and close leaf-surface detail is not strong enough for the target.

cam_tree_canopy_below.reason: A has the better living-leaf hue, but the choice involves a real tradeoff: B reveals more leaf/branch separation in the canopy interior. A compresses that area into murky dark olive. A is the preferred color/material direction, not an accepted final underside.
cam_tree_canopy_below.remaining: A fails shaded readability: upper-right and central under-canopy leaf clusters merge. Require a local material/light-response revision and matched below-canopy retest. Do not globally brighten the scene to conceal this.

cam_tree_canopy_edge.reason: A removes the chalky gray wash and makes the crown read as foliage. However, B has more tonal readability across the dense upper and right clusters. Neither balances material identity and shaded detail well enough.
cam_tree_canopy_edge.remaining: A becomes too uniformly dark through broad overlapping leaf patches. Outer leaf/branch contours show no obvious new rectangular halo or missing-crown defect, but alpha/raster stair-stepping remains visible in both. Motion and mip stability are unknown.

globalObservations: Better hue is a meaningful visible improvement, but does not establish improved leaf microstructure or natural transmission.
No obvious new gross shape/coverage loss, rectangular card borders or bright outline halo was observed in these full-resolution stills.
Dense dark underside/edge clusters are a readability regression relative to the paler variant. Preserve the improved hue while repairing this bounded problem.
Direct camera capture edge quality cannot establish ordinary native-player AA. No temporal, LOD or perf approval.
The user-authored orange tree remains unchanged context. No removal or recolor is recommended by this leaf review.

aaaComparison.reason: ARK still has stronger variation between illuminated leaf faces, warm transmitted light and readable shaded plant interiors, integrated ground layers, and clearer near/middle/far separation. The greener Ward direction closes a color-identity gap but still lacks those material/depth qualities. Palm morphology is not a required Ward target; compare rendering plausibility, not species shape.
aaaComparison.limits: ARK promotional stills have unknown camera, exposure, render scale, hardware and processing; subjects differ. No performance or animation parity claim.

nextEvidence: Retest the preferred green direction from below and edge with a bounded shaded-leaf response revision. Preserve frontlit hue and existing silhouette.
